solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 6 across to 5); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food cook carries is hot and cold

indicators.note: the falsified word holds the other letters within it, as a bag carries its contents

parts.note: to cook the books is to fake them
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps
C is the usual abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A recipe line: the dish the cook carries is served both hot and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a noun in the kitchen scene, but it is the verb meaning falsify, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried patty of flaked fish and potato is a simple everyday dish, so it counts as food.

clue.text: Loud competition enthralling any number in the country

parts.note: F stands for forte, loud in music

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the race holds the number inside it

parts.note: a race is a competition
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A loud competition in some country captivates countless people.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation of western Europe, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Without hesitation children get angry

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for children sits around the hesitation

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Children immediately lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside, so nothing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper, from the bull charging at red.

clue.text: Famous boxer had to work hand in glove

parts.note: Henry Cooper was a famous British heavyweight boxer
to have a meal is to eat it, so had means ate

explanation.surface: A famous boxer had to work closely with his trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cooper was a much-loved British heavyweight of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: To work hand in glove is to collaborate closely, which is what working together means.

clue.text: Adventurous wanderer in dark, English bishop bumping into German philosopher

indicators.note: the pieces force their way into the middle of the philosopher's name

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher
night is the dark
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: An English bishop in the dark bumps into a German philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval knight who roved in search of chivalrous adventures was an adventurous wanderer.

clue.text: Wish expressed for peace is false — look into it

indicators.note: the short word for look goes inside the word for false, which 'it' points back to

parts.note: a sham is something false or pretended
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a greeting of peace is insincere and urges a closer look.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew greeting means peace and is spoken as a wish for the other person's peace and wellbeing.

clue.text: Gasp when the ideal situation falls short

indicators.note: falling short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: heaven is a perfect or ideal state

explanation.surface: Someone gasps when a perfect situation turns out not quite perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls short' drops the last N from HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe heavily or pant with effort is to gasp; a heave is also a laboured breath.

clue.text: Europeans move slowly north carrying a box

indicators.note: the turned word holds the others inside it
in a down clue, going north means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to snail is to move slowly
the box is slang for the television

explanation.surface: Europeans crawl northwards carrying a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north' turns SNAIL upwards to LIANS, which carries A and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Latvia, a Baltic state, are Europeans.

clue.text: African galas may go wild

indicators.note: going wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Festive galas may get out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Madagascar, off the east coast, is an African.

clue.text: Great drink containing solvent

parts.note: ace is slang for great or excellent
tonic water is a drink, often with gin

explanation.surface: A tasting note: a great drink that happens to contain solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing solvent' reads as a description of the drink but is the definition: an adjective formed from acetone, the common solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a familiar solvent, as in nail-polish remover, so the adjective describes something containing it.

clue.text: Business group in vehicle reached by phone

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Tel is the standard abbreviation for telephone, as on letterheads

explanation.surface: Members of a business group meet in a car and are reached by phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is an association of firms that fix prices or output together, a kind of business combine.

clue.text: Army officer, subsequently fellow-fighter going side by side

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
later means subsequently
an ally fights on the same side

explanation.surface: An army colonel and, later, a comrade march side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in parallel or alongside, hence going side by side.

clue.text: Time to invade Indian island

indicators.note: the letter for time enters the middle of the people's name, as an invader enters territory

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American (Indian) people

explanation.surface: A historical scene: the moment comes to invade an Indian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island, in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Maybe maiden at home is sticking pig — a common household task!

indicators.note: the other pieces are stuck into the animal's name, like a skewer stuck in a pig

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a maiden is an example of an over in cricket, one in which no runs are scored
in means at home

explanation.surface: A grisly domestic scene: a girl at home sticking a pig, offered as a routine chore.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are conceded, hence 'Maybe' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a vacuum cleaner over the carpets, named after a brand, is a routine domestic chore.

clue.text: Terribly mean blokes do go on for many years

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: Mean blokes, terribly enough, seem to go on and on for years.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to live to a great age, so it is a colloquial way of saying to last a long time.

clue.text: One won't 2 (SEE RED), when this unemotional?

definitions.meaning: someone drained of blood would literally not see any red
describing a person who is cold and without passion

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who will not lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'see red' literally: with no blood, there is no red to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking vigour or feeling, a person can be called drained and cold, the figurative sense of the word.

clue.text: Cheap food of a former Chinese period sending a bad message?

parts.note: Spam is a cheap tinned meat
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: Cheap food from an old Chinese dynasty is sent as a bad message.
explanation.definitionFit: Spamming is sending unwanted junk emails in bulk, so a cryptic way of sending bad messages.

clue.text: After sound suggesting grumble, was first to be happy

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a grunt is a gruff sound of discontent
led means was in front, came first

explanation.surface: After grumbling, someone was the first to be happy.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUNTLED is a jocular back-formation from disgruntled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the playful opposite of disgruntled, it means pleased or satisfied.

clue.text: For each favourite, make allowance for bad act?

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
to ration is to allot a fixed allowance of something

explanation.surface: Giving each favourite an allowance is questioned as a bad act.
explanation.definitionFit: Committing a crime or misdeed is called carrying it out, so the noun names a wrongdoing done.

clue.text: Deviant reveals deplorable inclination, getting left out

parts.note: sad means deplorable, as in a sad state of affairs

indicators.note: the letter for left is omitted from the word

parts.note: a list is a tilt or inclination, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A deviant reveals a deplorable leaning when excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting left out' removes L from LIST to leave IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who enjoys inflicting cruelty is a kind of pervert, hence a deviant.

clue.text: Tedious folk gathered round good short-story teller

indicators.note: the tedious folk gather around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: bores are tedious people

explanation.surface: Tedious people gathered round a good storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: Jorge Luis Borges, the Argentine writer, was famous for his short stories.

clue.text: By battle site, disregard short priest

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a First World War battle; 'By' just places it first

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: to ignore is to disregard

explanation.surface: An instruction to ignore a short priest standing by a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter from IGNORE, leaving IGNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is an honorific given to senior Roman Catholic clergy, so it names a priest.

clue.text: This person's a success — a potential queen bee maybe?

parts.note: the setter referring to themself: I am, shortened to I'm
a go is a success, as in making a go of it

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being a success, a queen bee in waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult winged stage of an insect is the final form, so a queen bee is one such grown insect.

clue.text: Reproduced document shows Australia needing help after setback

indicators.note: a setback sends the letters backwards, read from right to left

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
aid means help

explanation.surface: A news line: a copied document shows Australia needs help after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after setback' turns OZAID round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy made by the diazotype process, an old way of duplicating plans, is a reproduced document.

clue.text: A yen to go on after ailments? Quite so!

indicators.note: the short pieces are placed after the word for ailments

parts.note: ills are ailments
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A yearning to carry on after illness is met with hearty agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic exclamation of agreement, like 'absolutely' or 'you bet'.

clue.text: Transient affair involves love ultimately out of this world

indicators.note: the word for affair wraps around the other letters, taking them in

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word love

parts.note: ET, the extraterrestrial, is literally from outside this world

explanation.surface: A short-lived affair involving love that seems out of this world.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing quickly is short-lived, which is exactly what transient means.

clue.text: French writer performing for old judge

parts.note: Andre Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate
on means performing, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: A French writer appears performing as an old judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gideon was one of the judges of Israel in the Old Testament Book of Judges.

clue.text: Gracious — regretful Miss has to hide extra-large plant!

indicators.note: the size letters are concealed inside the combined pieces

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like 'gracious!'
the Cole Porter song 'Miss Otis Regrets' makes Otis the regretful Miss
OS stands for outsize, an extra-large clothing size

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a sorry spinster has to hide an enormous plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Otis Regrets' is a Cole Porter song, so the regretful Miss is Otis; 'Gracious' is an exclamation, like 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Myosotis is the botanical genus of the forget-me-not, a small flowering plant.
